shell.guideTitle: A clear path to reconciled books
shell.guideDescription: Compare a complete settlement window across three sources.
shell.guide1Body: Upload orders, payment transactions and bank deposits using the exact CSV schemas.
shell.guide2Body: Select one snapshot of each kind. Checks run synchronously and preserve an immutable report.
shell.guide3Body: Inspect exceptions, source references and currency-separated values. Export the report for your team.
shell.guideNote: Sample Data uses the included synthetic CSVs. The app identifies differences; it never moves funds.

reconciliation.description: Follow every difference back to its source. Know exactly what needs attention.

imports.dropzone: Drop your CSV here, or browse files

imports.guideTitle: A clean start for your data
imports.guideDescription: Use a complete, consistent settlement window.
imports.guide1Body: Headers, column order and casing must match exactly. Extra columns are rejected.
imports.guide2Body: Use integer minor units: 10000 is BRL 100.00 or JPY 10,000. Supported: BRL, USD, EUR, GBP, JPY.
imports.guide3Body: IDs must be unique within a file. Refund transactions use negative gross values.
imports.atomicNote: Sample files are synthetic. Each upload is atomic; a rejected file creates no partial dataset. Imports and reports cannot be edited or deleted.
imports.historyDescription: Persisted source snapshots and their provenance

runs.title: Reconciliation runs
runs.description: Three datasets. One clear picture of your settlement window.
runs.selectWindow: Select three datasets from the same settlement window.
runs.guideDescription: Deterministic checks across the payment lifecycle
runs.guide1Body: Compare expected charges and refunds, including split payments. Identify missing payments and unknown orders.
runs.guide2Body: Compare transaction net amounts with bank deposits by payout reference. Keep different currencies separate.
runs.guide3Body: Save input identifiers, content hashes and the rules version. Selecting the same inputs returns the same report.
runs.syncNote: A run completes within the request. “Needs attention” means the checks finished and found differences to investigate.
runs.historyDescription: Saved reports with traceable source snapshots
runs.empty: No runs yet. Select your datasets above or explore Sample Data.

reports.warning: Differences are signals for investigation. A net total can hide offsetting errors; always inspect individual order and payout checks.

reports.multipleFindings: One record can contain multiple findings.

missing_payment.label: Missing payment
missing_payment.body: No charge in the expected currency was found. Check whether the order was paid and whether the payment export covers the full settlement window.

gross_mismatch.label: Payment amount mismatch
gross_mismatch.body: Charges in the order currency do not equal the expected gross amount. Review split charges and the original order value.

refund_mismatch.label: Refund mismatch
refund_mismatch.body: Observed refunds differ from the expected refund. Check refund timing and whether all refund transactions were included.

unexpected_order.label: Unrecognized order
unexpected_order.body: Payments reference an order that is absent from the selected orders dataset. Amounts cannot be compared until the source order is identified.

currency_mismatch.label: Currency mismatch
currency_mismatch.body: The record contains different currencies. Values remain separate; no exchange rate or currency conversion is assumed.

missing_settlement.label: Missing settlement
missing_settlement.body: A bank deposit references a payout with no payment transactions in the selected dataset. Check settlement references and the export window.

missing_deposit.label: Missing bank deposit
missing_deposit.body: A payout has payment transactions but no matching bank deposit. Verify the expected deposit date and bank payout reference.

net_mismatch.label: Deposit amount mismatch
net_mismatch.body: The bank deposit differs from charges minus refunds and fees. Check adjustments, withheld amounts and the settlement statement.

settings.title: Settings & connection
settings.description: Connect your local reconciliation service. Keep credentials on your machine.
settings.loopback: Loopback connections only · No browser-to-API CORS required
settings.addAddress: Add your local API address and key below.
settings.addressHelp: Use 127.0.0.1, localhost or [::1], with the port where FastAPI is running.
settings.keyHelp: Held in server memory for up to eight hours. Never stored in browser storage, URLs or logs. The field clears after each connection attempt.
settings.guide1Body: This is a local prototype, not a multi-tenant SaaS. Keep both servers bound to loopback. There are no user accounts or role-based permissions.
settings.guide2Body: The Next.js server calls FastAPI with X-API-Key. The browser receives an opaque HttpOnly, SameSite session cookie. A server restart clears session connections.
settings.guide3Body: Imports and reconciliation reports are immutable in the configured SQLite database. Resetting a connection does not delete financial data.
settings.environmentBody: For a persistent local setup, configure CLEARLEDGER_API_URL and CLEARLEDGER_API_KEY in the server environment. See the project README for startup and backup commands.
settings.sharedWarning: Before any shared deployment: add identity and access control, TLS, rate limiting and an operational security review.
